- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.1) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.1), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by +3–5% to avoid “too-low” traps.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ above recent high); apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 10–15% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend in history, model often fails to revert; add 2–4% upward bias to forecast to counteract over-downturn.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment volatility — smooth sentiment transitions before forecasting; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to weight forecast adjustments.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– spikes (e.g., +1.1, -1.1, +1.1), model often misreads momentum; apply “sentiment dampening” — reduce forecast amplitude by 10–15% for such cycles.
